## 3. An explicit physical capacity bound makes the correction small

Let \(M_1\) be the minus-ocean family whose filled outer plus contours have area at most \(R^2\), with no winding. A Dirichlet trial potential supported on \(M_1\setminus B\) gives an explicit capacity upper bound.

Set
\[
P_*=\lceil4R\rceil-8,\qquad q_c=8e^{-3\theta/2},
\]
\[
q_5=4e^{-\theta(2-\sqrt5/2)},\qquad
u_r=\frac{6nq_5^{2r}}{1-q_5},
\]
and
\[
m_c=\frac23\sum_{P\ge4}P(4e^{-5\theta/4})^P.
\]
For \(u_r<1\),
\[
\boxed{
\frac{C_\kappa}{Z_A}
\le U_C:=
\frac1{1-u_r}
\left[
\frac{(8n)^{10}q_c^{P_*}}{1-q_c}
+(n+\kappa)e^{-\phi(k_*-1-nm_c)}
\right].
}
\tag{2}
\]

The second term is essential: it accounts for configurations that reach nonnegative magnetization through many small droplets.

For sufficiently large fixed \(C\), the leading suppression is
\[
U_C\le
\operatorname{poly}_\theta(n,R)
e^{-(6\theta-4\log8)R}.
\]
The entropy subtraction \(4\log8\) is retained.

The exact core identity
\[
N_A=Z_A-\frac{C_\kappa}{\kappa}
\]
then yields, whenever \(U_C<\kappa\),
\[
N_\kappa\ge Z_A(1-U_C/\kappa).
\]
Combining this with (1),
\[
\boxed{
\frac{N_E}{N_\kappa}
\le
b_-+\xi+
\frac{\mathsf H k_*U_C}{1-U_C/\kappa}.
}
\tag{3}
\]

For \(r=O(\log(nR/\epsilon))\) and \(P_0=K_0R\),
\[
\mathsf H
\le
\operatorname{poly}_\theta(n,R,\epsilon^{-1})e^{aK_0R},
\]
where the entropy-count coefficient \(a\) remains bounded as the fixed temperature is lowered. Consequently, sufficiently large fixed \(\theta\) makes the last term in (3) small once
\[
R\ge K_\theta\log(nR/\epsilon).
\]

**Equation (3) is the strongest completed residence consequence.** Evaluating it requires polynomial work even though \(\mathsf H\) itself can be exponentially large. No exponentially long physical repair trajectory is required.

The same capacity bound also certifies
\[
T_h\ge U_C^{-1}-\kappa^{-1},
\]
which controls when the retained additive source error \(D_0\) is relatively negligible.
